verses.text: These are the terms of the covenant the LORD told Moses to make with the Israelites in Moab, alongside the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.
Moses called all Israel together and said, “You saw for yourselves everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, his servants, and his whole land.
You saw the great trials, the signs, and those incredible wonders with your own eyes.
Yet to this day the LORD hasn't given you a heart that understands, eyes that see, or ears that hear.
I led you through the wilderness for forty years. The clothes on your backs and the sandals on your feet never wore out.
You didn't eat bread or drink wine or any strong drink, so you'd know that I am the LORD your God.
When you reached this place, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan came out to fight us, and we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh.
So keep the terms of this covenant and put them into practice, so things will go well in everything you do.
Today all of you are standing in the presence of the LORD your God: your leaders, your tribes, your elders, your officers, and every man of Israel,
along with your children, your wives, and the foreigners in your camps, from those who cut your wood to those who draw your water.
You're here to enter the covenant of the LORD your God and bind yourselves by the oath he's making with you today.
Today he's establishing you as his people and becoming your God, just as he told you and swore to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
I'm making this covenant and oath with more than just you.
It includes those standing here with us today before the LORD our God and those who aren't here with us today.
You know how we lived in Egypt and how we traveled right through the other nations along the way.
You saw the detestable things among them, their idols made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.
So make sure no man, woman, family, or tribe among you turns their heart away from the LORD our God today to serve those nations' gods. Don't let a root that produces bitter poison grow among you.
Someone might hear the words of this curse and tell themselves, ‘I'll be fine even if I stubbornly go my own way.’ That would bring ruin to the well-watered land along with the dry.
The LORD won't pardon that person. The LORD's anger and jealousy will blaze against them, every curse written in this book will fall on them, and the LORD will erase their name from under the sky.
The LORD will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with every curse of the covenant written in this book of the law.
The next generation, your children who come after you, and foreigners who come from far away will see the plagues in the land and the sickness the LORD has inflicted on it.

They'll see the whole land burning with sulfur and covered with salt. Nothing is planted, nothing grows, and even grass can't sprout. It'll be like Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim when the LORD overturned those cities in his fierce anger.
All the nations will ask, ‘Why did the LORD do this to this land? What stirred up such fierce anger?’
People will answer, ‘They abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, that he made with them when he brought them out of Egypt.
They went off to serve and worship other gods, gods they didn't know and that he hadn't given them.
So the LORD's anger burned against this land, and he brought on it every curse written in this book.
In furious anger the LORD ripped them out of their land by the roots and threw them into another land, where they are today.’
Things kept secret belong to the LORD our God. What he's revealed belongs to us and our children forever, so we can live by every word of this law.”
